name: Kingdom of Cambodia
native: ព្រះរាជាណាចក្រកម្ពុជា (Preăh Réachéanachâkr Kâmpŭchéa)

predecessors.name: French Indochina
predecessors.text: Cambodia, independent from France on 9 November 1953

ledger.x: 1970: South Vietnamese and US forces enter eastern Cambodia (the Cambodian campaign, 29 April to 22 July): ARVN at the Parrot's Beak on 30 April, US forces at the Fishhook on 1 May (withdrawn by 30 June).
1970: the campaign ends (22 July) with the withdrawal of ARVN and US forces; ARVN's zone was later reduced to 'a depth of 10-15 km' (mid-1971).
1970: the monarchy is abolished and the Khmer Republic proclaimed (9 October) by Lon Nol, who had overthrown Sihanouk on 18 March 1970; same state, same colour (rule 2).

1972: North Vietnamese forces 'gradually and deliberately scaled back their presence' in Cambodia, leaving the insurgents (CPNLAF, the Khmer Rouge) in the north-east; the Civil War page says the combat was handed to the insurgents ('Khmerization') as their strength reached 35-40,000.
1972: the north-east passes to the Khmer Rouge and its fighting with the Republic.
1975: the war ends on 17 April, when Phnom Penh surrendered to the Khmer Rouge.
1975: Phnom Penh falls to the Khmer Rouge (17 April), after Lon Nol resigned and left on 1 April; the last Republic-held area, the Preah Vihear temple, falls on 22 May.
1993: the monarchy is restored (24 September) as the Kingdom of Cambodia, after the State of Cambodia (30 April 1989) and the United Nations administration (28 February 1992).
1993: Cambodia returns under its king after the UNTAC elections ('Monarchy restored: 24 September 1993').

wars.name: Cambodian campaign
wars.outcome: ARVN and US forces entered eastern Cambodia (29 April to 22 July 1970; US operations 1 May to 30 June) to destroy PAVN/VC sanctuaries and withdrew; the infobox lists 'Temporary occupation and subsequent withdrawal from eastern Cambodia by ARVN/US'.

wars.name: Cambodian Civil War
wars.outcome: Khmer Rouge victory: Phnom Penh surrendered on 17 April 1975 and the last Republic-held area fell on 22 May 1975.

certainty.note: A colonial-era surveyed frontier; the pages record Cambodia's borders recognised by the National Liberation Front and North Vietnam in 1967.
The war: the north-east and the countryside were held by PAVN and the Khmer Rouge without lines on any page.
The state is absent: the land belongs to Democratic Kampuchea, the People's Republic of Kampuchea and the State of Cambodia (other dossiers).

The page notes disputes with Thailand (Preah Vihear, 'unsettled since 1962'; armed conflict in 2025) and 'disagreements over some offshore islands and sections of the boundary with Vietnam', moving no line.
